annotation.title_clean: 미국 휴머노이드 로봇 산업 및 정책 동향과 시사점
annotation.title_en: U.S. Humanoid Robot Industry and Policy Trends and Implications
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kim, J. (Korea Institute for International Economic Policy, KIEP)
annotation.summary_en: KIEP briefing on the US humanoid robot industry and Trump second-term policy: AI executive orders, deregulation, export controls and outbound investment limits on China, onshoring. Compares US and China strengths and draws implications for Korea, such as building a physical-AI ecosystem and supporting the K-Humanoid Alliance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Global humanoid market projected to grow from $2.02B (2024) to $15.26B (2030), 39.2% CAGR.
China produced 87% of humanoids delivered in 2025 and holds 63% of key supply-chain firms; the US leads in AI chips and models.
Trump administration policy: AI executive orders, Action Plan, Genesis Mission, deregulation, onshoring; a robotics executive order is under consideration for 2026.
US counters China via export controls (BIS Entity List), outbound investment rules (OISP, COINS Act), CFIUS, and the DoD 1260H list including Unitree.
Korea should leverage appliance, auto and battery manufacturing to build a physical-AI ecosystem and strengthen the K-Humanoid Alliance.
